sections.name: a
sections.label: Meeting A, 2026-11-25
sections.content:
An unlabelled speech-to-text transcript of 824 lines, with house rules from the group's own conventions and eight supplied files. Result: 11 topics, 62 fragments, 5 attendance records, 17 decision points, 15 minutes, 2 decisions, 11 tasks, 10 references, 32 open questions; 53 fragments used as evidence, each carrying words copied by the tool. Every stage reply was accepted at the first attempt and all 17 document checks pass.

Against the group's hand-written minutes (11 items, 2 decisions): every item covered, both decisions matched, a third go-ahead flagged for the secretary to rule on (it became a formal decision the next day), and four matters the hand-written minutes left out.

sections.name: b
sections.label: Meeting B, 2026-10-27
sections.content: 669 lines, run from the bundle alone with no attendee list and no files: 43 fragments, 15 decision points, 17 minutes, 1 decision, 8 tasks, 29 open questions; all checks pass. The first stage had two replies refused as malformed JSON before the third was accepted. The hand-written minutes have three decisions; the run recorded one as a decision and left the other two as a record and a discussion.

sections.name: trial
sections.label: The first trial, and what it changed
sections.content: A first run of meeting A sliced the transcript into 21 fragments of up to 98 lines and marked almost every decision point ambiguous, so it drafted no decisions. Two changes to the package fixed both: a rule that the moment something is agreed is a fragment of its own with a 40-line limit, and a definition of ambiguous that does not count a missing owner or an unknown speaker. With no attendee list that run marked all four members and the contractor as mentioned, none present, and asked who was there.

sections.name: limits
sections.label: Limits
sections.content: One model (Sonnet, headless), one run per meeting, no measure of variance. The comparison with hand-written minutes is a reading, not a score. Nothing has been used by the group itself. The real runs are kept outside any repository because the transcripts are private.
